230350101.text: *sigh* I want to go back to Inazuma... How could this happen to me...

230350104.text: Traveler? *sigh* Don't even mention the novel. Those researchers working on Genius Invokation TCG are barely holding it together.

230350105.text: According to a researcher I know quite well, the team encountered all kinds of problems that could only be described as baffling...

230350106.text: For example, a Haravatat researcher suddenly asked a question one day.

230350107.text: He said that if the effect descriptions on the cards are too long, it might discourage people who aren't used to reading long blocks of text from playing the game.

230350108.text: Researchers are used to reading large chunks of text and aren't affected by this issue, but the long descriptions could very well turn potential players away.

230350109.text: So he suggested cutting the amount of text on some cards in half to make them easier to read.

subQuests.subQuestName: Meet up with Fukumoto at Puspa Café

230350302.text: Look at his outfit, his hairstyle, and that hair color... This is exactly what a protagonist in a card game novel should look like!

230350304.text: Heh, just trust my instincts on the market. But now's not a good time to explain...

230350309.text: Traveler, please ask Cyno to be the model for my novel... I'm counting on you!

230350306.text: Really? That's great. I'm working on the third book of "King of Invokations," and this time, I'm not going to base it on the gameplay mechanics of Genius Invokation TCG.

230350307.text: I'm going to create an all-new way of playing. For instance... I could get all cards to be suspended mid-air on the field. Players will have to collect cards as they consider their next move, all the while preventing their opponent from collecting cards themselves...

230350308.text: Hahaha! I'm getting excited just thinking about it! But we don't have time for this right now...

230350401.text: ...Hmm, this combination of cards isn't so bad.

230350402.text: But they're not strong enough to deal with quick attacks...

230350403.text: What are you up to, Cyno?

230350404.text: #{NICKNAME}? I didn't expect to see you here.

230350405.text: I'm in the middle of trying to build a Genius Invokation deck with a relatively slow attack speed.

230350406.text: I'm hoping that the deck would allow the player to obtain an abundance of resources and plenty of powerful cards...

230350407.text: But to be honest, it's hard to build a deck like that...

230350408.text: Currently, in the Genius Invokation TCG community, some players prefer to use cards with fast attack speeds.

230350409.text: At the beginning of the game, they play a large number of cards in one go in order to swiftly defeat their opponent.

230350410.text: But I'm no fan of this tactic. I prefer to continuously accumulate resources in different ways...

230350411.text: Seizing every possible opportunity, building up my advantage, and eventually securing the victory...

230350412.text: Yes, yes! Wonderful! You're just like the main character in my novel!

230350416.text: Hello, General Mahamatra. I don't suppose you've heard of me...

230350417.text: I've read your novel. It's very good.

230350419.text: In the novel, every time the protagonist is at a disadvantage, he always manages to get a card that wasn't in his deck through various means, then defeats his opponent. This left a lasting impression on me.

230350420.text: I understand that writing novels requires taking a creative license, but this way of winning is a departure from the fundamental mechanics of Genius Invokation TCG.

230350421.text: About that, well... Although I do play Genius Invokation TCG a lot, I'm not really good at it... And if you write about the duels with a competitive mindset, it wouldn't make for an interesting story.

230350422.text: Hmm, is that so? Well, as luck would have it, I've just built two decks of cards, so we can play a few rounds of Genius Invokation TCG here. Maybe you'll find some inspiration.

230350501.text: You take several pictures of Cyno very quickly...

230350601.text: This has been a big help. I'm sure Asagiri will make an excellent illustration!

230350602.text: Thank you very much, Cyno. I'll be sure to send you a copy of the novel as soon as it's published.

230350603.text: Uh, Cyno, the two decks you're holding are...?

230350604.text: Didn't you promise to play a few games of Genius Invokation TCG with me earlier?

230350605.text: Eh!? I—I'm not very good at it, so uh... Traveler! You're definitely better than me!

230350608.text: Then the matter is settled. Here, take this quick attack deck.

230350609.text: I'm going to use this relatively slower deck to see how I can deal with your attacks.

230350701.text: Cyno, your play style is so... slow and deliberate...
